To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate at which non-conservative substitutions occur in proteins is systematically promoted by molecular chaperones in the cell.
the evolutionary rate of non-conservatives substitutions in proteins is systematically influenced by chaperones and disorder.
the rate of nonconservative substitutions is promoted in disordered regions and rewired proteins, and is inversely proportional to the assistance by chaperones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of protein disorder and molecular chaperones in protein network evolution.
the evolution of proteins, and more precisely with the evolution of the proteome.
the interplay of protein disorder and molecular chaperones during the evolution of protein networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay between chaperones and intrinsically disorded proteins promotes the evolution of protein networks.
chaperones and disorder play an important role in promoting the evolution of protein networks.
our results show that molecular chaperones are important for the evolvability and robustness of protein networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interplay between molecular chaperones (which assist in protein folding and stability) and protein disorder (which is a major feature of many protein interactions and functions) promotes the evolution of protein networks.
chaperones and intrinsic disorder are both crucial to enable the evolution of new functions in proteins and protein networks.
the interplay of chaperones, protein disorder, and protein interactions provides a general framework to understand the evolution of protein networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular chaperones promote protein evolution by buffering destabilizing mutations, and that the interplay between chaperones and intrinsically disorded proteins is crucial in this regard.
the interplay of protein disorder and molecular chaperones is crucial in enabling the evolution of protein networks.
the interplay of molecular machines and the intrinsic disorder of proteins promotes the evolvability and evolution of protein networks.
